questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution guarantees the Right to Equality?
questions.explanation: Article 14 states: 'The State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.'

questions.question: Which Article abolishes untouchability?
questions.explanation: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form. Enforcement of any disability arising out of untouchability is a punishable offence.

questions.question: Within how many hours must an arrested person be produced before a magistrate?
questions.explanation: Under Article 22(2) of the Constitution, every arrested person must be produced before the nearest magistrate within 24 hours of arrest.

questions.question: Which is called the 'Heart and Soul' of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar called Article 32 (Right to Constitutional Remedies) the heart and soul of the Constitution.

questions.question: What is the helpline number for women in distress in India?
questions.explanation: 181 is the Women Helpline number operational 24/7 across India for women in distress.

questions.question: Under the POSH Act, within how many months must a complaint be filed?
questions.explanation: Under the POSH Act 2013, a written complaint must be filed within 3 months of the incident (extendable to 6 months in certain cases).

questions.question: How many weeks of paid maternity leave is a woman entitled to for her first child?
questions.explanation: The Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act 2017 provides 26 weeks of paid leave for the first two children.

questions.question: Which section of BNS deals with cruelty by husband/relatives?
questions.explanation: Section 85 of BNS (formerly 498A IPC) deals with cruelty by husband or relatives of husband.

questions.question: What is the National Consumer Helpline number?
questions.explanation: 1800-11-4000 is the toll-free National Consumer Helpline for filing consumer complaints.

questions.question: What is the maximum claim amount for District Consumer Forum?
questions.explanation: Under Consumer Protection Act 2019, District Commission handles claims up to ₹1 crore.

questions.question: Where can you file a consumer complaint online?
questions.explanation: Both consumerhelpline.gov.in (for grievances) and edaakhil.nic.in (for formal complaints to consumer forums) can be used.

questions.question: Can police refuse to register an FIR for a cognizable offence?
questions.explanation: Under Section 173 BNSS (Section 154 CrPC), police CANNOT refuse to register an FIR for cognizable offences. If they do, complain to the SP or Magistrate.

questions.question: What is a Zero FIR?
options: FIR filed at any police station regardless of jurisdiction
questions.explanation: A Zero FIR can be filed at ANY police station, irrespective of where the offence occurred. The FIR is later transferred to the concerned police station.

questions.question: What replaced the Indian Penal Code (IPC) in 2024?
questions.explanation: BNS (Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita) 2023 replaced IPC from 1 July 2024. BNSS replaced CrPC, and BSA replaced Indian Evidence Act.

questions.question: If chargesheet is not filed within 60 days (for offences up to 7 years), the accused gets:
questions.explanation: Under BNSS, if chargesheet is not filed within 60 days (offences up to 7 years) or 90 days (7+ years), the accused is entitled to default bail as a matter of right.

questions.question: What is the cybercrime helpline number in India?
questions.explanation: 1930 is the Cyber Crime Helpline. Call within the 'golden hour' of a fraud for best chances of recovering money.

questions.question: Where can you report cybercrime online?
questions.explanation: cybercrime.gov.in is the official National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal where you can file complaints online.
